title: Manuel Manetta, Jelly Roll Morton gone, and picnics at the fairground
summary: Professor Manetta inspired and taught Morand and still teaches today, playing trumpet and trombone at once. Jelly Roll had left town. Summer picnics at the fairground featured brass and string bands.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Well, do you remember many of the trombones from that time? Well, no, I don't, I don't remember many of them. I mean, you spoke of Jack Carey, do you remember Ori? Was he playing down here then? No, he had left too, I think. Or, uh... Did you ever have anything to do with Professor Mineta, Manuel Mineta? Yeah, Old Horse they called him, eh? Yeah.
Well, he inspired me a whole lot. And, uh, used to show me a few things on the trumpet. Yeah.
Was he more of a teacher or a regular musician? He's still teaching today, yeah. Must be pretty old.
And he features blowing the trumpet and the trombone at the same time. I heard him not quite long ago.
Uh, do you remember any of the pianists? Was a jelly roll still in New Orleans at the time?

No, no, he had left a jelly roll. I don't remember much of him. You played, I imagine, a lot of picnics and... Oh, yeah. In the summertime we were playing picnics. At that time the fairground, we used to get picnics at the fairground. That's when I first heard Lewis a whole lot. Uh, you used to have two bands. A brass band and a big hall and a string band and, uh, at least a jazz band and a small hall.
